002-space-taller.title: Space Makes You Taller. Then It Hurts. 🚀 #shorts
lines: Go to space, and you come back taller.
Without gravity pressing down, an astronaut's spine stretches out.
On long missions, they can grow up to three percent taller. That's about two inches.
But it hurts. More than half of US astronauts report back pain during their missions.
And back on Earth, gravity wins. Within a few months, the extra height is gone.

003-coldest-survivor.title: Her Body Cooled to 13.7 °C. She Survived. 🧊 #shorts
lines: Her heart stopped for hours. And she survived.
In nineteen ninety-nine, a young doctor, Anna Bågenholm, fell through ice while skiing in Norway.
She found an air pocket. But after forty minutes in icy water, her heart stopped.
When rescuers finally pulled her out, her body temperature was just thirteen point seven degrees Celsius.
In Tromsø, a machine slowly warmed her blood. Hours later, her heart beat again.
She recovered, and went back to work as a doctor.

004-death-zone.title: Above 8,000 m, Your Body Starts Dying 🏔️ #shorts
lines: Climb above eight thousand meters, and your body starts to die.
Each breath brings about a third of the oxygen you get at sea level.
Up here, your body can't adapt. It just keeps getting weaker.
Your heart races, even while you rest.
Fluid can leak into your lungs. Your brain can swell.
That's why most climbers on Everest breathe bottled oxygen.
Climbers have a name for it. The death zone.
